flags.issue: The big jump only covers the right third of the frame. The boarded-up shell becomes the izakaya (awning, paper lanterns, noren, round window, planters, side stall), but the stairs, the bridge and the overall cold blue-grey lighting are pixel-identical to stage 0, so the scene doesn't feel transformed, just has one building swapped. The new crosswalk is made of broken, staggered white blocks that float on the reflective water and read as debris, not zebra stripes.
flags.fix: Make the crosswalk solid, evenly spaced, continuous bars running across the road as in the end image. Have the stage 1 jump also warm the key light toward amber and add at least one change on the left half, such as warm LED strips on the stair treads or lit shop windows behind the stairs, so the whole frame changes.

flags.issue: No visible change from stage 1. Once rain noise is filtered out the frame is identical.
flags.fix: Give this stage its own visible step, e.g. warm under-tread lights on the foreground staircase.
Add a distinct step, e.g. a blue neon strip along the bridge underside, as in the end image.
Add a distinct step, e.g. warm-lit storefront windows on the left wall beside the stairs.
Add a distinct step, e.g. potted plants and a chalkboard sign at the foot of the stairs.
Add a distinct step, e.g. ivy and wisteria hanging over the bridge railing.

flags.issue: The only new element is a thin string of fairy lights far behind the bridge railing. Each bulb is a few pixels wide, it sits above the parapet and not on it, and it can't be noticed at this angle.
flags.fix: Run the string lights along the near bridge railing and canopy, with bigger and brighter bulbs plus white paper lanterns hanging off the bridge as in the end image, so they read at street level.
Add a distinct step, e.g. the neon coffee-cup sign on the bridge side, or the warm glow on the stair treads.
Add a distinct step, e.g. pink vertical kanji neon on the cafe building's right edge.

flags.issue: No visible change from stage 9. That makes nine stages in a row (2-10) of dead air.
flags.fix: Spread the stage 11-12 content and the missing end-image elements across stages 2-10 so every stage shows something new.

flags.issue: Ivy, wisteria and lit upper windows on the cafe are a real, visible step. It is the first real change in ten stages, so it reads as a sudden catch-up and not as one step in a steady progression.
flags.fix: Keep it, but move part of the greenery (the awning-level ivy) to an earlier stage so the facade grows over time.

flags.issue: Adds a blown-out cyan-white glowing slab at the top of the cafe. It has no readable lettering or shape, it doesn't match the end image's pink 茶房 vertical neon, and it washes the whole upper frame in cyan haze. The finale still lacks warm stair lighting, bridge lanterns and vines, the coffee-cup neon, the bridge underside strip, the left-side lit shops and the overall amber grade, so it ends at about half of the target.
flags.fix: Replace the glow slab with a vertical pink kanji neon sign of controlled brightness, without a bloom flood. Make sure the last stage has every end-image element: warm-lit stair treads, lanterns and wisteria on the bridge, the cyan underside strip, the coffee-cup neon, lit left storefronts and a warm amber color grade.

verdict: Fails as a progression. The stage 0 to 1 jump is big and partly satisfying (the dead shuttered building turning into a lantern-lit izakaya is the right idea), but it is limited to one building, and the crosswalk it adds is a broken scatter of floating tiles. After that, stages 2-10 are effectively frozen: the only change is a nearly invisible string of lights at stage 7. Stages 11-12 then cram in facade greenery and a blown-out cyan glow. The left half of the frame (stairs, bridge, left storefronts), which dominates the end image with warm light, lanterns and wisteria, never changes, and the cold blue grade never warms. The final stage sits at roughly 48/100 of the target.
